extracted.intended_audience: users of the Singular computer algebra system (mathematicians, computational algebraists, and programmers)
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of function-level documentation from the Singular manual (purpose, syntax, behavior notes, examples) for users calling these library/system functions. Focused on function semantics and usage guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: preimage
rubrics_metrics.description: Preimage handles ideals (not polynomials); the result of a preimage calculation of a principal ideal is the (closure of) the preimage of the ideal, not that of the polynomial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows mapping between rings and computing preimage of ideals; kernel(r,f) returns the kernel of map f. Note emphasizes that preimage semantics operate on ideals and the returned ideal must be an ideal in the target ring. See referenced sections for map, ideal, kernel.

rubrics_metrics.name: prime
rubrics_metrics.description: prime(int_expression) returns the largest prime less than or equal to the argument; returns 2 for all arguments smaller than 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: prime(320000) -> 319993; prime(32004) -> 32003; prime(0) or prime(-1) -> 2. See related int and general lib sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: primefactors
rubrics_metrics.description: primefactors(int/bigint/number expression [, int bound]) returns the prime factorisation up to an optionally given bound b on the prime factors; returns a list describing prime factors, multiplicities and residual n'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When called with integer types, no ring needs to be active. For number inputs they are assumed to be integers in a polynomial ring over Q. Returned structure: L[1][i]=i-th prime factor (ascending), L[2][i]=multiplicity, L[3]=n' (sign/zero/rest). Examples show behavior with and without bound and how output is arranged.

rubrics_metrics.name: print
rubrics_metrics.description: print(expression) prints the expression; print(expression, "betti") prints graded Betti numbers from a matrix; print(expression, format_string) returns printed output as string according to format string.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supported format strings: "%s", "%2s", "%l", "%2l", "%;", "%t", "%p", "%b" (each with described behavior). Examples show printing modules, converting to strings, and printing Betti matrices. Note: "betti" is not a format string for the generic form (it's a special second-argument mode). See many related sections for conversions and betti.

rubrics_metrics.name: printf
rubrics_metrics.description: printf(string_expression [, any_expressions]) performs formatted output using a format control string; outputs to standard out (no return).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format specifiers similar to print; %n and %2 produce newline without consuming an argument. If an additional argument is a list, wrap it in list() to avoid flattening. Examples show formatted printing of rings, lists, matrices, and use of special conversions "%p", "%;", "%b". See fprintf, sprintf, print for related functionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: prune
rubrics_metrics.description: prune(module_expression) returns the module minimally embedded in a free module such that the corresponding factor modules are isomorphic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If input has attribute "isHomog" set, prune sets it as well. For non-global orderings, only reduction steps with constant units are performed so returned module may not be minimal. Example shows pruning a module to minimal generators. See module section.

rubrics_metrics.name: qhweight
rubrics_metrics.description: qhweight(ideal_expression) computes the weight vector of the variables for a quasihomogeneous ideal; returns intvec of zeros if input is not weighted homogeneous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ideal x4+y3+z2 returns 0,3,4,6 for ring with parameter t. See related sections on ideal, intvec, weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: qrds
rubrics_metrics.description: qrds(matrix_expression, [number arguments]) computes all eigenvalues (with multiplicities) of a real matrix using the numeric QR double shift algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumes ground field complex and all matrix entries real (imaginary part zero). Returns list with two lists: distinct eigenvalues and their integer multiplicities. If algorithm fails returns list with single entry 0. The numeric arguments control deflation detection, Heron's iteration threshold, and equality tolerance for considering eigenvalues equal (suggested tiny value like 10^(-100)). Example provided for a 3x3 matrix over complex ground field with high precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: quote
rubrics_metrics.description: quote(expression) prevents expressions from evaluation; used for write to ssi links to avoid evaluation before sending to another Singular process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within a quoted expression, quote can be undone by eval (each eval undoes exactly one quote). Example shows write(l, quote(std(eval(i+j)))) usage and subsequent read/eval. See Ssi links and eval documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: quotient
rubrics_metrics.description: quotient(I,J) for ideals returns {a ∈ R | aJ ⊂ I}; quotient(M,J) for modules returns {b ∈ R^n | bJ ⊂ M}. Signatures for ideal/module/module-ideal are supported and return ideal or module accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show ideal and module quotient computations and returned generators. References to fglmquot, ideal, module sections for related tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: random
rubrics_metrics.description: random(int a, int b) returns a random integer in [a,b]. random(int bound, int rows, int cols) returns an intmat with absolute entries ≤ bound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Random generator can be seeded with system("random",seed) or via command line option; current generator value accessible by system("random"). Internally generator runs in 1..2^31-2 with full period; max-min must not exceed 2^31-2. Examples show seeding reproducibility and intmat form output.

rubrics_metrics.name: rank
rubrics_metrics.description: rank(matrix_expression) returns the rank (int) of a matrix over the ground field; rank(matrix,1) uses row-echelon based method, default uses LU decomposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works by computing row echelon form using same algorithm as ludecomp. Example shows rank of random 100x100 matrix. See ludecomp for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: read
rubrics_metrics.description: read(link_expression [, string_expression]) reads data from a link; for ASCII links returns whole file content as string; for ssi links reads one expression and returns it after evaluation; for DBM links returns entries or keyed values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For ASCII links empty string reads from standard input. For ssi links read blocks until data available (use status to check). DBM links: one-arg read returns next entry; two-arg read returns value for given key. Example shows writing an ideal to a file and reading it back into an ideal via execute("ideal k="+read("save_i")+";"). See link, execute, getdump, status, write.

rubrics_metrics.name: reduce
rubrics_metrics.description: reduce(...) reduces a polynomial/vector/ideal/module to its normal form with respect to an ideal/module represented by a standard basis; returns 0 iff the first argument belongs to the ideal/module. Many overloads and optional flags available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional int third argument modifies behavior: 0 default; 1 consider only leading term (no tail reduction); 2 tail reduction (local/mixed ordering: reduce also with bad ecart); 4 reduce without division (may return non-zero constant multiple of remainder). If second argument is poly or matrix, p is replaced by p/u (works only for zero-dimensional ideals), and optional degree bound and weight vector may be given. If second argument is not a standard basis the result may have no meaning. Commands reduce and NF are synonymous. Examples illustrate different behaviors and multi-argument usage (e.g., normal form of 1/(1+x) mod x^3 up to degree 5). See division, ideal, module, std, vector.

rubrics_metrics.name: regularity
rubrics_metrics.description: regularity(list_expression_or_resolution) computes the Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity (int) of a homogeneous ideal/module from a minimal resolution given by the argument; for non-minimal resolution returns an upper bound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition: regularity is smallest s with deg(e_{a,i}) ≤ s + i for all i in a minimal resolution. If res or mres inputs are homogeneous the regularity is computed and used as degree bound unless option(notRegularity) is set. Examples show computing regularity from resolutions and how non-minimal resolutions yield upper bounds. See related res, minres, mres, resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: repart
rubrics_metrics.description: repart(number_expression) returns the real part of a number from a complex ground field; returns its argument otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: repart(1+2*i) -> 1. See impart for imaginary part counterpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: res
rubrics_metrics.description: res(ideal_or_module, int_length [, any]) computes a (possibly minimal) free resolution of an ideal or module using a heuristically chosen method. The second argument k specifies the length; if ≤0 assumed number of variables of basering. Third argument, if given, minimizes the returned resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depending on input type the method chosen is: nres for quotient rings, lres for homogeneous ideals with k=0, sres for not minimized resolution / local rings / homogeneous input with k≠0, mres otherwise. Accessing single elements of resolution may require partial computations. Examples illustrate which method is used for various inputs (homogeneous, local, inhomogeneous). See fglm, lres, mres, nres, sres, minres.

rubrics_metrics.name: reservedName
rubrics_metrics.description: reservedName() prints list of all reserved identifiers; reservedName(string) tests whether string is a reserved identifier (returns int 1/0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes blackbox/newstruct types. Examples: reservedName("ring") -> 1, reservedName("xyz") -> 0. See names and string sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: resultant
rubrics_metrics.description: resultant(poly f, poly g, ring_variable) computes the resultant of f and g with respect to given variable and returns a polynomial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example computes resultant(f,g,x) for polynomials in ZZ/32003 ring. See poly and ring sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: ringlist
rubrics_metrics.description: ringlist(ring_expression) decomposes a ring/qring into a list of 4 (or 6 for non-commutative) components, similar to ring_list but first entry differs: components describe field description, variable names, monomial ordering blocks, and quotient ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field description encodes characteristic/type/precision/imaginary unit or nested ringlist for extensions; variable names as list of strings; monomial ordering as list of blocks where each block lists ordering name and parameter intvec; quotient ideal included. Note explaining that data depending on a ring belong to current ring and will be mapped via fetch. Examples show modifying ringlist to construct a new ring and setting minpolys. See ring_list and qring.

rubrics_metrics.name: ring_list
rubrics_metrics.description: ring_list(ring_expression) decomposes a ring/qring into a list of 4 components (field description as cring, variable names, monomial ordering blocks, quotient ideal); identical to ringlist except first entry content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to capture ring structure and reconstruct rings via ring(list). Examples parallel ringlist usage (modifying field to ZZ/p, adding variables, changing ordering blocks). See ringlist and qring.

rubrics_metrics.name: rvar
rubrics_metrics.description: rvar(name|poly|string) returns the number of the variable if the argument refers to a ring variable of the basering; returns 0 otherwise (usable in boolean contexts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: rvar(x) -> 1 in ring with variables (x,y,z); rvar(r) -> 0; rvar(var(3)) -> 3; rvar("x") -> 1. See defined, var, varstr, ring sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: sba
rubrics_metrics.description: sba(ideal_expression [, int module_order_variant, int rewrite_order_variant]) returns a standard basis of an ideal using optimized signature-based algorithms (variants of Faugere's F5), with optional control over internal module order and rewrite order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Second argument selects internal module order used by sba (0: induced Schreyer, non-incremental; 1: position-over-term, incremental; 2: term-over-position, non-incremental; 3: Schreyer-weighted degree...). Third argument selects rewrite order variant (0 or 1 referencing two papers/DOIs). Default sba(i) ≡ sba(i,0,1). Correctness guaranteed only for global orderings; timing for pure lex may be slow — recommendation: compute basis in graded reverse-lex then convert to lex with fglm/grwalk; if memory issues try other std algorithms (std, groebner, slimgb). Behavior may differ significantly with variant choices; examples demonstrate incremental vs non-incremental usage and homogenization.

rubrics_metrics.name: setring
rubrics_metrics.description: setring ring_name changes the basering to another (already defined) ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes of basering within a procedure are local to that procedure; use keepring to move a ring up one nesting level if needed. Example toggles basering between r1 and r2. See keepring and qring/ ring sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: simplex
rubrics_metrics.description: simplex(matrix M, int n, int m, int m1, int m2, int m3) performs the simplex algorithm on tableau M describing a linear program; returns a list with solution tableau, status code, basis/non-basis mappings and sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumptions: ground field (real,N) with N>=4; M size m x n; m=m1+m2+m3; certain entries non-negative; variables non-negative; constraints encoded row-wise. Output L where L[1] is matrix tableau, L[2] status (0 finite, 1 unbounded, -1 no solution, -2 error), L[3] mapping of rows to variables, L[4] non-basis variables per column, L[5]=m, L[6]=n. Solution readable from first column of L[1]. Example demonstrates constructing tableau and calling simplex. See simplexOut in solve.lib for output formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: simplify
rubrics_metrics.description: simplify(obj_expression, int rules) returns a 'simplified' version of the object (poly, vector, ideal, module) according to bitwise simplification rules encoded in the integer argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Available rule bits and meanings: 1 normalize (divide by leading coefficient if unit); 2 erase zero generators/columns; 4 erase copies of earlier generators; 8 erase scalar multiples of earlier generators; 16 ground: erase generators whose leading monomials are copies with unit coeffs; 32 erase generators whose leading terms are divisible by leading terms of others; 64 normalize coefficients of every monomial. The default combinations produce different behaviors; examples show effects on ideals and matrices. Automatic conversion of matrix->module may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: size
rubrics_metrics.description: size(argument) returns an int whose meaning depends on argument type: for ideals/modules returns number of (non-zero) generators; for string/intvec/list/resolution returns length (number of characters/entries/elements); other types have type-specific meanings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supported argument types: string, bigint, number, intvec, intmat, poly, vector, ideal, module, matrix, list, resolution, ring. Examples omitted but documentation points to type-specific behavior; see corresponding sections (ideal, module, vector, etc.).
